findings.title: Created field and harmful actualization
findings.claim: The phrase places harm within the field of what has been brought into being: شَرِّ names the harm, while خَلَقَ supplies the created field whose forms, conditions, or capacities can become harmful in operation or occurrence.
findings.mechanism: The harm term carried by شَرِّ meets the later action and danger specifications, while the creation branch carried by خَلَقَ names the field in which those specifications occur. Their contact separates the created domain from the harmful realization and changes the phrase from a flat totality into a relation between bearer, condition, and harmful actualization.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the refuge request as covering harm arising within created things and situations, while keeping the ordinary created-field wording intact.
findings.containment: The primary reading remains refuge from the evil of what was created. The finding leaves live the supplied boundaries in which harm is attributed to directed human action, divine permission, decree, or intended outcome; it does not turn creation itself into a moral verdict.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run finding is reinforced by a legacy reader activation and exact connection rows; the reader source is qualified, and several counter-attributions remain live.
